title: Console: card-bundle triage and minimum shipping spec for dashboards, tracing, and cost views
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: We need to reduce scope and produce a tightly bounded shipping artifact that delivers usable console insights for the first alpha without incurring large telemetry or backend costs. This ticket defines which dashboard cards, tracing primitives, and cost breakdown snippets are in-scope for the Minimum Shipping Spec (MSS), and which items are deferred. The goal is to enable fast validation with customers and partners while preserving upgrade paths for richer tracing and per-token cost analysis in follow-ups.
background: Multiple prior PRDs asked for a broad surface of dashboards, an in-console flamegraph trace explorer, and per-request cost drilling. Early feasibility work shows the tracing UX and full-detail cost pipeline would require ~3x effort and add significant telemetry ingestion costs. We must prioritize pieces that unblock product validation: actionable anomaly indicators, route-level cost deltas, and lightweight span counts for triage. This is a scoped compromise to accelerate an alpha release and limit backend changes required for Dedicated/Private deployments.
scope_inclusions: Top-level 'Health & Cost' card showing 3 KPIs: latency P95, error rate, and rolling 7-day cost delta
Per-route compact cost delta card (percent change and absolute delta) with sparkline and link to route details
Lightweight tracing indicator: span count histogram and recent slow-request sample link (no flamegraph)
Sampling config UI stub (read-only) and a documented default sampling rate for alpha
Acceptance-ready telemetry contracts (proto) for the reduced card set to avoid downstream schema churn
scope_exclusions: Full interactive flamegraph explorer and span-level waterfall view
Per-token cost attribution and per-token timestamps
High-cardinality attribute filtering in the alpha dashboards
Long-retention raw trace storage in the alpha (beyond 7 days)
acceptance_criteria: Alpha console exposes the Health & Cost card with correct values computed from validated telemetry within 5% of reference dashboard numbers
Per-route cost delta card is present, clickable, and navigates to a route detail page that surfaces last-24h/7d comparisons
Tracing indicator shows span counts and surfaces one slow-request sample; clicking the sample opens a read-only, preformatted trace JSON blob for debugging
Telemetry contract tests (unit/integration) exist and pass in CI; schema version increment documented
Alpha does not increase estimated telemetry ingress costs beyond the agreed budget line item for the release (finance sign-off obtained)
tradeoffs: Excluding flamegraphs reduces developer ergonomics for deep triage but drastically cuts backend storage and UI work
Per-token cost exclusion prevents precise cost allocation to model variants but keeps rollout velocity and avoids upstream billing changes
Keeping sampling read-only simplifies alpha rollout but will require a follow-up to allow customer-tuneable sampling in Dedicated/Private
implementation_notes: Backend: implement aggregated metrics endpoints (route-level) that bucket by 1h and 24h windows; avoid raw-span indexing for alpha
Frontend: implement a compact card component reusable across dashboard and route list; wire open/close states to route details
Telemetry: add schema v2-lite in the proto repo and create a migration plan for existing producers
Docs: single-page alpha guidance that explains the limited scope and the planned follow-ups (sampling controls, flamegraphs, per-token breakdown)
test_plan: Unit tests for new aggregation endpoints with synthetic traffic fixtures
Integration test that verifies route-level cost deltas using replayed telemetry traces
E2E smoke test that loads the dashboard and asserts presence and basic interactions for the three KPIs
Load test for telemetry pipeline to ensure alpha ingestion rate keeps cost projection within budget
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal dogfood in nightly for 48 hours with monitoring targets and rollback hooks
Stage 2: opt-in alpha for 5 external customers (selected via solutions team) with dedicated feedback channel
Stage 3: GA gating decision based on SLA stability, telemetry cost delta vs projection, and customer feedback
Rollback criteria: sustained >10% increase in ingestion cost or unresolvable alert storm in first 24 hours
